subject: track.set_arm on the MCU rung: whether a request for a state sets it, against a Rec button that toggles on every press
question: When track.set_arm falls back to the MCU, does arming and then disarming a track leave it in the requested state each time, confirmed by a read of the track?

reverify.expected: the arm reaches the MCU rung (write_source mcu); arming answers State A with observed true and the refreshed track list reads the track armed; 30 reads of the track list 100 ms apart with no refresh all read it armed; disarming answers State A with observed false and the track list reads it disarmed; the track ends disarmed
reverify.cost: needs LPM_EVIDENCE_ROOT exported as an absolute path outside the repository, a running Logic with a project open and the Mackie Control surface bound; starts two servers; arms and disarms one track and leaves it disarmed

method: The release binary at 2d66c40de21a13e7caf06704fd0b0e3193b52e6f was started against the open project with LOGIC_PRO_MCP_ARM_KEYCODE set to a value that does not parse and nothing else talking to Logic. The harness armed the first disarmed track through logic_tracks arm, checked that the reply came from the MCU rung, refreshed the cache and read the track's isArmed from logic://tracks, read it 30 more times 100 ms apart without a refresh while Logic's Rec LED blinked, then disarmed it the same way. A second server started without the variable put the track back. Before the run Logic was quit, its AppleLanguages preference was set to this language, and the lpm-locale-campaign fixture was reopened with live_993_plugin_root_menu_in_every_locale.switch_to.
conclusion: On track 0 the arm reached the MCU rung after the Accessibility rung refused arm_key_config_invalid. It answered State A with observed True, and the track list read isArmed True; read 30 more times without a refresh, it read the track armed 30 times. The disarm answered State A with observed False, and the track list read isArmed False. All three checks passed.
limits: Only record-arm reaches the MCU rung this way. The run sets LOGIC_PRO_MCP_ARM_KEYCODE to a value that does not parse, so the Accessibility key rung refuses arm_key_config_invalid, which is not terminal. Mute and solo have no such setting; their MCU rung is covered by the unit tests only.

Only a state that differs from the request reaches the MCU. When the track already holds the requested state, the Accessibility rung answers a verified no-op first, so the MCU's own 'already set' branch is not driven live.

The track-list reading is isArmed from logic://tracks. Since this change the poller finds the record-enable checkbox with the same locator the handler's readback uses (AXLogicProElements.trackArmControl), so it is a second read at a later time, not a second way of finding the control.
The parser still writes isMuted and isSoloed from the Mute and Solo LED frames. Whether Logic blinks those LEDs as it blinks Rec was not measured.
One track of one fixture, one arm and one disarm per language, one host.
The binary without this change was run only in Korean; in this language there is only the reading of the fixed binary.

canon_not_applicable.reason: This record states a fact about the server's BEHAVIOUR -- which reply an arm or disarm request gets on the MCU rung against the track state read afterwards -- not about a string Logic ships. The only values it quotes are reply fields, a track index and booleans.
